144.0.0.en: Blessed be the LORD my rock, who teacheth my hands to war, and my fingers to fight.

144.0.1.en: 1- David thanks the mighty God, who gave him strength in fighting against the enemies. And because God is firm and strong like the rock, He is able to make David firm and strong in the battles against his enemies.

144.0.2.en: 2- God taught and trained David, so He gave him victory over a lion and a bear, and after this He gave him courage to triumph over Goliath, which qualified him for victory over all his enemies surrounding his country, so the kingdom expanded in his days, as God promised, from the river of Egypt to the Euphrates.

144.0.3.en: 3- God trained David for fighting so that he might defend himself and deliver his people from Goliath and the Philistines and all the enemies. By this training his faith in the mighty God who was with him was confirmed and he was filled with strength, and he triumphed over his sins and weaknesses.

144.0.4.en: 4- Faith in God's power and obedience to Him make it easy for a person to learn from God victory over Satan gradually in the spiritual battles, so that the person grows and becomes strong, and even becomes firm and victorious always. This means that the cause of the strength and victory is God, who was with David and works in all who trust in Him.

144.1.0.en: My goodness, and my fortress; my high tower, and my deliverer; my shield, and he in whom I trust; who subdueth my people under me.

144.1.1.en: High tower (sarh): a lofty building, or a great tower.

144.1.2.en: Shield (mijanni): the mijann is the large shield, and the shield is an ancient defensive instrument that the soldier used; it is a piece of wood with a handle at the back into which he put his hand, and he moved it before his face and body to protect him from the arrows of enemies.

144.1.3.en: 1- David describes God with many attributes: He is mercy, the refuge in which he takes shelter, and the high tower in which he fortifies himself, so that He delivers him from the hands of his enemies; He is the shield that protects him, and He is the one in whom he trusts, and who gives him strength and awe so that his people submit to him, and not only his enemies. He attributes every power in his life to God, who is the source of all blessings.

144.1.4.en: 2- The people that submit to a person are his senses and all his abilities, his body and spirit, his mind and emotions; that is, God gives him a strong will that leads him in the way of righteousness and goodness, protects him from the demons and defends him, so that he lives at peace within God his strong fortress, and thanks Him every day for these great mercies.

144.2.0.en: (vv. 3, 4): LORD, what is man, that thou takest knowledge of him! or the son of man, that thou makest account of him?

144.2.1.en: Man is like to a breath: his days are as a shadow that passeth away.

144.2.2.en: David marvels at God's concern for him, so he says that he is a weak man, and compares himself to a breath that a person breathes out, or the shadow of anything that passes with time. That is, he is something very small, so how does God care for him and think of him?

144.2.3.en: Here the divine knowledge means concern and care. And thinking means divine providence and care for all the needs of man. David marvels at God's humility and love in His concern for him and for every person.

144.2.4.en: Would that you, my brother, thank God every day for His care for you, for He is the source of every blessing in your life. So humble yourself before Him and before all His children, mankind, and your thanksgiving will increase, and God's gifts to you, and your inner joy.

144.3.0.en: Bow thy heavens, O LORD, and come down: touch the mountains, and they shall smoke. Cast forth lightning, and scatter them: shoot out thine arrows, and destroy them.

144.3.1.en: Bow (tati): condescend and bend down with humility.

144.3.2.en: 1- David begs God to condescend from His heights to care for His children and deliver them from their enemies; as for the enemies, that is, the demons, however strong and great they are like mountains, He touches them with His power and they smoke, that is, they begin to burn. And He shines upon them with His mighty light, so they fear and are scattered and flee from before His face, and when they flee He directs His arrows at them and they are greatly troubled. All this shows David's faith in the mighty God, whom no one can resist, so the weakness of the enemies before Him appears.

144.3.3.en: David does not look at his weakness before the power of the enemies, but at the power of God that is with him, which is able to crush the enemies.

144.3.4.en: 2- God's power appeared when He appeared to Moses and the people on the mountain, accompanied by smoke, fire, thunder, lightning and a thick cloud (Ex 19:16-19). These manifestations show the power of God and the weakness of man.

144.3.5.en: 3- These two verses speak of the Incarnation of Christ, who condescended from His heights. Although He fills heaven and earth, He became incarnate, lived among us, died on the Cross, and bound Satan.

144.3.6.en: And Satan burned before Him like smoke, and fled and was troubled. The arrows are a type of the Apostles, who spread the teachings of Christ that caught souls.

144.4.0.en: Send thine hand from above; rid me, and deliver me out of great waters, from the hand of strange children; whose mouth speaketh vanity, and their right hand is a right hand of falsehood.

144.4.1.en: 1- David asks God, who is above all, on high, that is, in the heavens, to deliver him from the great waters, by which he means the enemies, who are strangers to him. And those who speak false words, and whose right hand is false, that is, their speech is against the truth and their deeds are wicked; these are the wicked and the heretics in every generation, and everyone who resists the truth.

144.4.2.en: 2- The hand of God that was stretched out from on high is the incarnate Christ, who redeemed us from the great waters, that is, the demons who are strangers to us, and from their false speech and their vain deeds.

144.5.0.en: I will sing a new song unto thee, O God: upon a lyre of ten strings will I sing praises unto thee. It is he that giveth salvation unto kings: who delivereth David his servant from the hurtful sword.

144.5.1.en: 1- When David saw God's delivering power for him he rejoiced, and praised God with a new song, because it is full of new joys on account of the experiences and wonderful divine works that happened to him. His song was accompanied by a musical instrument, the lyre of ten strings, which signifies the ten commandments that David believed in, and the senses of man and his inner abilities. And he sang giving thanks to God, who saves devout kings like him, however weak he is, so that He kept the hurtful sword away from him, by which he means the sword of the great Goliath, for David threw Goliath to the ground with a small stone, then cut off his head with his sword.

144.5.2.en: 2- The new song is a type of the New Testament, and the ten strings are a type of the ten commandments. All the children of God in both Testaments sing with joy at His Incarnation and redemption; in the Old Testament they lived on hope and awaited the Messiah, and in the New Testament they saw the salvation offered on the Cross, so God's work in both Testaments is complete, because the whole Holy Bible speaks of Christ.

144.5.3.en: God, your God, is strong and able to deliver you from every evil, so take refuge in Him and do not fear Satan, his power and his wiles, for God will crush him and drive him away from you, so that you may continue your spiritual striving and enjoy fellowship with God.

144.6.0.en: Rid me, and deliver me from the hand of strange children, whose mouth speaketh vanity, and their right hand is a right hand of falsehood: that our sons may be as plants grown up in their youth; that our daughters may be as corner stones, polished after the similitude of a palace.

144.6.1.en: 1- Here David shows the good things and blessings of God that He gives His children after delivering them from the hands of their strange enemies, and from all their false deeds. And these blessings are many: the first is that He gives them plants grown up in their youth, that is, they have spiritual and bodily strength, and continue to grow, so that they may afterward lead their families and defend them against every evil. As for the daughters, he likens them to corner stones polished in the temple of the Lord, and the corner stone is that which binds all the stones of the two walls, and by this he means that the daughter is the one who will become a mother and bind all the members of her family to one another in love and unity. And these pillars are polished, that is, refined, and he means that the daughter should have a good, refined upbringing, so that the family lives as a temple for the Lord and worships the Lord in holiness and purity. Strong sons and holy daughters full of love are the most precious gift that God gives His people.

144.7.0.en: That our garners may be full, affording all manner of store: that our sheep may bring forth thousands and ten thousands in our streets:

144.7.1.en: 1- The second blessing for the people of God is that their storehouses be full of different kinds of grain. This means that God blessed their farming, so it produced abundant crops, and they gathered them into their storehouses to satisfy them.

144.7.2.en: 2- The storehouses of a person are his heart and mind, and God fills them with longing for Him, love of virtue, and every good thought and feeling toward God and people.

144.7.3.en: 3- The third blessing is in livestock, specifically in sheep, that they be many, for they multiply abundantly until they fill the streets with their numbers, and they obtain their products of milk, meat and wool... The sheep are a type of spiritual possessions, that is, the many souls that they draw to the Lord.

144.8.0.en: That our oxen may be strong to labour; that there be no breaking in, nor going out; that there be no complaining in our streets.

144.8.1.en: Laden (muhammalah): carrying young in the womb.

144.8.2.en: 1- The fourth blessing is in the cattle that God blesses, so they bear many young and are good cattle, and although they are desirable cattle, God keeps them from any breaking in, whether by predatory animals or by any attack of enemies, so they graze in the streets and the places around the houses in safety and peace. The laden cattle are a type of the spiritual blessings within a person, so that he is full of many graces.

144.8.3.en: 2- The fifth blessing is the peace in which the people of God and all their possessions live, and no one troubles them. This is a type of God's protection of His children from the wars of the demons, so that they may live with Him and grow spiritually.

144.9.0.en: Happy is that people, that is in such a case: yea, happy is that people, whose God is the LORD.

144.9.1.en: 1- At the conclusion of the psalm David declares his blessing on the people of God, that is, how joyful and happy they are; not only because of material good things, but because their source is God, so the people enjoy fellowship with God who dwells in their midst, and thank Him at all times and praise Him.

144.9.2.en: God's blessings upon you are many, but the greatest blessing is God's dwelling within you, so enjoy speaking with Him, and rejoice in His presence within you, and you will taste the sweetness of the Kingdom while you are on earth.

144.9.3.en: Glorifying the greatness of the Lord A song of praise. Of David "I will extol thee, my God, O king; and I will bless thy name for ever and ever" v. 1 Introduction:

144.9.4.en: 1- Its author: the prophet David, as appears from the title of the psalm.

144.9.5.en: 2- This psalm is a praise of God, as appears from the title. And all its verses praise God.

144.9.6.en: 3- This psalm and the psalms that follow it are psalms of praise, that is, from Psalm 145 to Psalm 150. The Book of Psalms ends with the praise of God, which is preparation for and entrance into eternity.

144.9.7.en: 4- This psalm is arranged according to the Hebrew alphabet, and each verse begins with one of the letters of the alphabet. And each verse consists of two parts, as will appear in the explanation of the psalm.

144.9.8.en: 5- This psalm is liturgical, that is, it was prayed in the congregational Jewish worship. It is prayed twice in the day and once in the evening, that is, three times every day, to glorify God and praise Him.

144.9.9.en: 6- The Divine Liturgy in the Church quotes from this psalm (v. 15), that is, it is prayed in the congregational worship in the New Testament.

144.9.10.en: 7- This psalm begins with David's praise of God and ends with the praise of all creation to Him, for the psalm calls everyone to praise God.

144.9.11.en: 8- This psalm is not found in the Agpeya.

145.0.0.en: I will extol thee, my God, O king; and I will bless thy name for ever and ever. Every day will I bless thee; and I will praise thy name for ever and ever.

145.0.1.en: 1- King David feels that God is the true King, and He is the King of kings; therefore he declares his submission to God in extolling Him, blessing Him and praising Him, and he even expresses his feeling continually every day, that is, throughout the days of his life, and indeed throughout the whole day, in his joys and his sorrows, in the time of rest and the time of trouble.

145.0.2.en: 2- David feels a special relationship between himself and God, so he says my God, for he has the boldness of sonship and a strong love for God, and his continual praise continues forever. Having enjoyed praise on earth, he longs for continual praise after putting off the body, to rejoice forever with God. It is implicitly understood that whoever has not experienced praise on earth will not long for continual praise in heaven, or will have no share in the Kingdom of Heaven.

145.0.3.en: 3- These two verses are read on the second day of the Feast of the Cross (18 Tut), because Christ reigned on the Cross; therefore we praise Him and bless Him because He is the Redeemer and Savior of mankind. It is understood from this that this psalm is liturgical in the Church, that is, it is used in the congregational worship.

145.1.0.en: Great is the LORD, and greatly to be praised; and his greatness is unsearchable.

145.1.2.en: 1- The praise of God is continual forever, because His greatness has no end; no man can search it out or reach its end.

145.1.3.en: 2- When David magnifies God he lifts his eyes to heaven, so he clings to heavenly things and rises above earthly lusts, and humbles himself before God, whose infinite greatness he cannot fathom to its depths.

145.2.0.en: One generation shall praise thy works to another, and shall declare thy mighty acts. I will speak of the glorious honour of thy majesty, and of thy wondrous works. And men shall speak of the might of thy terrible acts: and I will declare thy greatness. They shall abundantly utter the memory of thy great goodness, and shall sing of thy righteousness.

145.2.1.en: I will speak (alhaj): I meditate and speak continually.

145.2.3.en: The praise of God is from age to age, that is, from generation to generation, so it is continual throughout the generations, and even to the age to come, that is, in heaven, and that for many reasons, which are:

145.2.4.en: 1- Your works: which are very many and appear in His creation, living and inanimate; man, animals and plants.

145.2.5.en: 2- Your mighty acts: that is, Your great power, which is above every power in the world, which shattered the gods of Egypt, parted the Red Sea, and overcame all the gods of the pagan nations.

145.2.6.en: 3- Your majesty and glory: praised by the heavenly and the earthly, and no man can bear to see it, as Moses felt when he pleaded to see God (Ex 33:20-23).

145.2.7.en: 4- Your wondrous works: which appear in the order of Your creatures, whether in the body of man and his spirit, the arrangement of the system of the heavenly bodies, and the ecological balance between the various kinds of animals and the different plants.

145.2.8.en: 5- Your terrible acts: God is very awesome and fearful, and this appeared on few occasions, because man could not bear it; it appeared to Moses and the people on the mountain with smoke and fire, the thick cloud, and the sound of the trumpet and thunder. And the fear of Him leads a person to leave sin and to live a pure life. And His terrible acts appear in many great works, such as the heavenly bodies, the wide sea, the thunders and lightnings.

145.2.9.en: 6- Your greatness: which appears in the union of great awe with great tenderness, for although the angels cover their faces from the brightness of His glory, He at the same time cares for the smallest of His creatures, such as insects and small plants. He is perfection in everything.

145.2.10.en: 7- Your goodness: that is, all good, who feeds all flesh and cares for all His creatures, and in Him is perfect purity, love and every virtue.

145.2.11.en: 8- Your righteousness: You reject evil and are repelled by it, and despite Your great mercy, You are also great in Your righteousness. Righteousness and mercy were joined in Christ Jesus on the Cross.

145.2.12.en: How great and how sweet it is to meditate on the attributes of God and His many kindnesses, until the meditation turns into thanksgiving and praise that fills the heart with joy and spreads happiness in the whole atmosphere around it.

145.3.0.en: The LORD is gracious, and full of compassion; slow to anger, and of great mercy. The LORD is good to all: and his tender mercies are over all his works.

145.3.1.en: 1- Although God is awesome, just and great, He is at the same time loving and merciful, and His love appears in His longsuffering and tenderness. God's mercy is mingled with all His works. When He is just and fearful and firm, He is also merciful, as He permitted the bondage of His people in Egypt, but brought them out with a great power. And as He permitted their humiliation in the age of the Judges because of their worship of idols, He had mercy on them when they cried to Him, and sent them judges who freed them from bondage.

145.3.2.en: 2- The goodness of God and His mercy are over all men, righteous and wicked; His sun and His air and His gifts are for all, that they may know Him and live with Him, and He is good to all His creatures, feeding the wild beasts and the tame animals. He has mercy on and cares for the smallest of creatures.

145.4.0.en: All thy works shall praise thee, O LORD; and thy saints shall bless thee. They shall speak of the glory of thy kingdom, and talk of thy power; to make known to the sons of men his mighty acts, and the glorious majesty of his kingdom. Thy kingdom is an everlasting kingdom, and thy dominion endureth throughout all generations.

145.4.1.en: 1- All the works of God, that is, His creatures, glorify Him through their submission to the divine order, so they walk in the order appointed for them, and this amazes men, so they praise God. As for the devout, they know God and utter His praise, so they enjoy fellowship with Him. And they speak of God's reign over all creatures, and praise Your great power.

145.4.2.en: 2- As the devout praise by their words and deeds they proclaim to all men the greatness of God, which lasts throughout life, and even forever.

145.4.3.en: Your thanking God every day for His dealings with you is a quiet preaching of the great God, who gives blessings to all men. By this thanksgiving you quietly invite everyone to glorify God.

145.5.s.en: (3) The mercy of the Lord to those who fear Him

145.5.0.en: The LORD upholdeth all that fall, and raiseth up all those that be bowed down.

145.5.2.en: Raiseth up (muqawwim): brings back to the straight way.

145.5.3.en: God's mercy appears in its first form, which is the support of those who fall, and of the bowed down, the repentant who return to God. God rejoices in the repentant, and is even tender toward those who do not repent, and warns them that perhaps they may repent. He is a tender Father who strives for the salvation of His children, and forgives them their falls if they repent.

145.6.0.en: The eyes of all wait upon thee; and thou givest them their meat in due season. Thou openest thine hand, and satisfiest the desire of every living thing.

145.6.1.en: 1- The second form of God's mercy is satisfying the needs of men, and indeed of all living creatures. He satisfies all, from the small insect to the predatory beasts, and above all man, the head of creation, and He gives man not only material satisfaction but also psychological, so that he is content and thankful to God, and above every satisfaction He gives spiritual satisfaction. He is satisfied with God's love the nearer he draws to Him.

145.6.2.en: 2- We pray these verses in the Divine Liturgies in the Litany of the Airs of Heaven, the Waters and the Plants, and we also pray them at the end of the Second Hoos, which is (Ps 136).

145.7.0.en: The LORD is righteous in all his ways, and merciful in all his works.

145.7.1.en: The third form of God's mercy is its association with righteousness. God's mercy is not for pampering man and spoiling him, but to lead him to righteousness and goodness. A person may need God's mercy to discipline him at times, or to withhold from him some of his desires, so that it may raise him up, and he may live in righteousness.

145.8.0.en: The LORD is nigh unto all them that call upon him, to all that call upon him in truth. He will fulfil the desire of them that fear him: he also will hear their cry, and will save them.

145.8.1.en: 1- The fourth form of God's mercy is His nearness to men, for He is not a God who exalts Himself and keeps away from His creation, but a loving Father who draws near to His children to give them His love.

145.8.2.en: 2- Those who enjoy the feeling that God is near them are:

145.8.3.en: a - those who call upon Him in truth, that is, who make requests according to God's will, and He answers them.

145.8.4.en: b - they fear Him, so they walk uprightly and reject sin, and if they fall they hasten to repentance.

145.8.5.en: God is present everywhere, but everyone who draws near to Him feels His nearness, and calls upon Him in truth, and fears Him. And whoever draws near to God, God draws near to him and answers his requests. And whoever does God's will, God fulfils his desires and forgives his sins.

145.9.0.en: The LORD preserveth all them that love him: but all the wicked will he destroy.

145.9.1.en: The fifth form of God's mercy is His preserving everyone who loves Him, so He keeps him from dangers and problems that exceed his ability, and brings him through in peace on the way of life. On the contrary, He is just, so He destroys all the wicked who trouble His children, and supports His children in all their steps.

145.10.0.en: My mouth shall speak the praise of the LORD: and let all flesh bless his holy name for ever and ever. He concludes the psalm with praising God with his understanding and heart, and by this praise he stirs the hearts of those who hear him, so God blesses them too, and thus the earth is filled with the praise of God.

145.10.1.en: Look at God's mercy upon you and meditate on it until it leads you to have mercy on those around you, so that you do not judge them or become angry with them, but find excuses for them, and if you can, pray for them and support them with your works of love, so that you draw their hearts to God.

145.10.2.en: Praise of God the Shepherd "Hallelujah. Praise the LORD, O my soul" v. 1 Introduction:

145.10.3.en: 1- Its author: unknown, because this psalm has no title; it is one of the orphan psalms whose author is unknown, but there are two other opinions:

145.10.4.en: a - that its author is David.

145.10.5.en: b - there is a title in the Septuagint translation, "Prescribed with Hallelujah, of Haggai and Zechariah," so some see that the author is Haggai and Zechariah.

145.10.6.en: 2- When was it written? According to what we mentioned about its author, there are two opinions:

145.10.8.en: b - after the return from captivity.

145.10.9.en: 3- This psalm is among the Hallel psalms, which are the five psalms from (Ps 146 to Ps 150), and they are distinct from the Egyptian Hallel psalms (Ps 113-118) and from the two psalms of the Great Hallel (Ps 135, 136).

145.10.10.en: 4- These Hallel psalms (Ps 146 to Ps 150) begin and end with the word Hallelujah, except (Ps 147), which begins with the word "Praise," which also means exultation.

145.10.11.en: 5- There are some other psalms, apart from the Hallel psalms (Ps 146 to Ps 150), that begin and end with the word Hallelujah, and they are: Ps 106, Ps 113, Ps 135. (And there are other psalms that only begin with the word Hallelujah, and they are: Ps 111, Ps 112.) (And there are other psalms that only end with the word Hallelujah, and they are Ps 104, 105, 116, 117.)

145.10.12.en: 6- This psalm and all the Hallel psalms are considered liturgical, for they were prayed after the return from captivity and were also prayed in the Jewish synagogues that spread in the land of Judea in the two centuries before the birth of Christ, and remained until the first century AD.

145.10.13.en: 7- This psalm suits every believer who feels God's care for him in his needs and weaknesses, so he praises Him and thanks Him for His kindnesses.

145.10.14.en: 8- This psalm is found in the Agpeya in the prayer of Sleep, where a person thanks God and praises Him for His gifts throughout the day.
